findings.location: §109.1 append/restart rules and §109.3 crash-prefix acceptance, approximately lines 128 and 153
findings.title: Recovery cannot distinguish a complete synced frame whose response was lost from an acknowledged frame
findings.evidence: The acceptance rule says only acknowledged frame boundaries may load and a complete unacknowledged frame must fail globally. A crash after frame Sync but before response acknowledgement leaves identical bytes to a crash after acknowledgement; an extra durable acknowledgment record has the same crash window.
findings.recommendation: Define a complete valid Sync'd frame as the journal linearization point. Restart accepts any complete valid prefix and callers converge by re-reading current case state; short/partial/corrupt frames and truly uncertain chains remain fail-closed. Do not require recovery to infer response delivery.

findings.title: Unused ready cases have no legal cleanup transition
findings.evidence: A ready case may only transition to open_recovery_required in the table, while cleanup_quarantined is reachable only from open_recovery_required, committed, terminal_failed, or quarantined. Routine cleanup of a successfully provisioned but never-started case is unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Define an authorized locked cleanup path from ready, either directly to cleanup_quarantined or via a semantically appropriate quarantine state, then add the transition to allowed/forbidden matrix tests.

recommendations: Treat successful full-frame Sync as the durable state linearization point.
Define restart behavior after Sync error when bytes nevertheless form a valid full chain.
Add an unused-ready cleanup transition and tests.
